newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Petroz to develop Timor Sea oil.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Petroz to develop Timor Sea oil.

text.p: Petroz NL said on Wednesday that its board has approved development of the Elang and Kakatua oil projects in the Timor Sea.
Petroz has a 14.95 percent interest in the ZOCA 91-12 permit which covers the Elang and Kakatua fields, which is in the Timor Sea Zone of Cooperation between Indonesia and Australia.
The other joint venture partners are The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd with 42.42 percent, Santos Ltd with 21.43 percent and Indonesia's Inpex Sahul Ltd with 21.21 percent.
Petroz said the fields had total proven and probable reserves of about 17 million barrels of oil.
The fields would be developed using subsea completions and a floating production, storage and offloading (FPSO) vessel.
Of the many options considered by the joint venture, this concept would provide the most cost-effective development and would generate the highest return on the project, Petroz said.
The development plan would now be submitted to the joint Australia-Indonesia authority for the area for approval, it said.
"Once approval has been granted, Petroz expects field development to be undertaken during 1997 and early 1998, with first oil production by mid-1998," the company said.
Petroz said its share of the capital cost of the project would be A$13 million, to be fully funded by part of the proceeds of a recently completed A$41 million rights issue.
"The cash flow generated from Elang and Kakatua production will be strategically important to the company," Petroz managing director Rod Brown said in a statement.
"It will contribute to Petroz' share of the costs of developing the Bayu - Undan gas condensate field as well as supporting the company's exploration programmes," he said.
